BLOCKER: `deploy/plane-a/terraform/aws/main.tf` creates `aws_eks_cluster` but omits `aws_eks_node_group` compute resources, causing all Helm stack pods on AWS to remain stuck in `Pending` state.

`deploy/plane-a/helm/product-forge/templates/configmap.yaml` hardcodes `POSTGRES_HOST` to the local StatefulSet service, leaving no configuration mechanism to connect `core-api` to the managed RDS/Cloud SQL databases provisioned by Terraform.
MAJOR: `scripts/dev/plane_a_deployer.py` health probe defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/health` without setting up port-forwarding or resolving cloud load balancers, causing health checks to fail and trigger rollback on remote deployments.

Sensitive credentials (`change-in-production-vault`, static auth tokens) are hardcoded across Helm `values.yaml`, `secret.yaml`, and Terraform variable defaults without enforcing secret generation or external secret providers.
MINOR: Subprocess output handling in `plane_a_deployer.py` (`proc.stdout[-1000:]`) truncates CLI logs, which can obscure critical terraform and helm failure diagnostic details.
NIT: Terraform variable declarations for database credentials lack input validation rules (e.g. minimum length or complexity constraints).
SUMMARY: Turnkey cloud deployment fails end-to-end on AWS/GCP due to missing EKS compute nodes, disconnected cloud database endpoints in Helm templates, and unrouted local health checks.
Add `aws_eks_node_group` to AWS Terraform, make Helm database endpoint configurable for managed DBs, and implement port-forwarding in the deployer script before approval.
